title: Organizational and Economic Obstacles to Automation: A Cautionary Tale from AT&T in the Twentieth Century
eligible_reason: The design qualifies: binary post_cutover switches on at each city's first dial cutover date, with city FE and census-year FE, three effective treated cohorts (first treated census 1920, 1930 or 1940) plus cities never treated by the 1940 census, estimated with reghdfe. However, every main-text regression (15 columns in Tables 3, 4(a), 4(b); 'Table 3, 4.do' line 206) absorbs c.ln_citypop##i.year, i.e. a time-varying control (log city population measured at each census) and its interaction with year FE. Under PROTOCOL Section 2 ('Excluded: time-varying controls') no reported specification is eligible as published. The state-by-year FE (i.statefip##i.year) alone would be allowed. n_eligible_specs is therefore 0; the 15 candidate specifications are listed under ineligible_specs with full detail in case the lead decides a no-population-control variant is acceptable.
design_notes: Stata package (Code/__run_all.do runs Figure 1, Figure 2, Table 2, Table 3-4, Table 5-6). Only 'Table 3, 4.do' contains DiD regressions; Table 5 is descriptives by cutover-date bin and Table 6 is a cross-sectional regression of any_cutover / earliest_cutover on 1910 city characteristics. Data: individual complete-count census records of telephone-industry workers 1910-1940 (1900 dropped), collapsed to city x census year occupation counts; merged to city-decade populations and to city cutover dates combining AT&T archival records (164 large cities) and newspaper reports (887 cities). Timing: census_year set to 1910.29, 1920.00, 1930.25, 1940.25; cutovers coinciding with a census date shifted by 0.01. Treatment is absorbing. In the raw cutover file 214 distinct cutover dates (>=1917) exist, but with decennial outcomes the effective cohorts are: first post-cutover census 1920 (11 cities), 1930 (236), 1940 (425); 122 cities cut over after the 1940 census and 29 never (these are never-treated within the panel; counts are before the population/balance restrictions). Clustering by city. No weights in main-table columns. reghdfe + estout.
estimators_reported: TWFE static (reghdfe) with state-by-year FE and log city population x year FE
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 3 effective census-period cohorts (first treated census 1920/1930/1940); 214 distinct underlying cutover dates
modern_estimator_note: Full-text flags mention Borusyak and Callaway, so the article likely discusses or reports them, but the package code contains no did_imputation/csdid; if an appendix uses them it is not in the package.

ineligible_specs.treatment_var: post_cutover = (census_year >= earliest_cutover); earliest_cutover = city's first dial cutover date (year + month/12) from AT&T archives and newspapers (lines 143-163)
ineligible_specs.time_var: year (census years 1910, 1920, 1930, 1940; census_year = 1910.29, 1920.00, 1930.25, 1940.25 used for timing)
ineligible_specs.fe: id (city) + year (census year) + i.statefip##i.year (state-by-year) + c.ln_citypop##i.year (log city population and its interaction with year FE)
ineligible_specs.controls: ln_citypop (time-varying log city population from City-decade Population.dta) and c.ln_citypop#i.year; state-by-year FE
ineligible_specs.weights: none (the [aw=population] branch at line 202 applies only to pct_* outcomes, none of which are in the main tables except pct_of_oper_f1_y0, which is explicitly routed to the unweighted branch)
ineligible_specs.sample_condition: telephone-industry workers (ind1950==578) in 1910-1940 complete-count census, ages 16-65, occ1950!=1000, collapsed to city x census year; cities with dated cutovers only (drop earliest_cutover>=2000) and no pre-1917 cutover; NYC boroughs dropped; balanced panel (4 census years); min citypop>=500; citypop1920<=100000. N = 10,852 city-years (2,713 cities) for most outcomes; 10,580 for Table 4(a) cols 3-4; 4,986 for workers:managers ratio
ineligible_specs.data_file: Data/Telephone Industry Workers.dta + Telephone Worker occstr-indstr.dta + City-decade Population.dta + Cutovers-AT&T Data.dta + Cutovers-Newspaper Data.dta (sample built in the do-file)
ineligible_specs.exclusion_reason: time-varying control: c.ln_citypop##i.year (log city population by census year, and its interaction with year FE). Would be eligible if this term were dropped (state-by-year FE is allowed).
